title: SubmIT — A guide to the project year
overview: These locally generated guides follow one synthetic project, the School Garden Sensor, through the application. Start with the guide for your role and follow its links. Every image is captured from the real testing application at desktop size 1440 × 1000. All names and content are synthetic; credentials are never published. English controls are used and explained. Preparation creates two supporting accepted projects and a valid rubric through authorized APIs. Initial valid rankings and provisional final grades are prepared only as technical read prerequisites, not represented as UI actions. The main idea, its revision, and later decisions are completed through the actual interfaces.

schueler.title: Student guide
schueler.intro: Prerequisites: a student account and, later, a finalized group assignment. In this story student01 creates the main idea; student02 and student03 also apply. The same project continues through each role and stage.

chapters.title: Account and workspace
chapters.text: Create a student account on `/register` with **Create account**, or sign in on `/login` with **Sign in**. Never publish passwords. Your personal workspace is `/`. On `/settings`, edit **Account name** and choose **Save changes**. The account name does not change the username or role. An administrator assigns classes and elective subjects; see [account administration](administration.md#accounts).

images.alt: Personal workspace for the signed-in synthetic student account
images.caption: The workspace belongs to the authenticated student.

images.alt: Administration view of synthetic account and class settings
images.caption: Account administration is available only to an authenticated administrator.

chapters.title: Create and submit an idea
chapters.text: On `/ideas`, choose **＋ New idea** and complete **Title**, **School year**, **Description**, **Intended outcome**, and **Initial scope points**. Use **Find students by display name** and **Add** to invite up to four additional owners. The creator manages collaborators under **Details & history**. **Save draft** saves changes; **Edit** reopens the draft; **Submit** sends it for review. Editing is unavailable during review. **Withdraw** is an alternative, not the successful path. Teachers may create ideas but may not review their own work. Continue to [teacher review](lehrkraefte.md#idea-review).

images.alt: Saved School Garden Sensor idea draft with edit and submit actions
images.caption: A saved draft can be edited before submission.

images.alt: Submitted main idea in the student account
images.caption: After submission, another teacher reviews the same idea.

chapters.title: Respond to feedback and complete the specification
chapters.text: After **Request revision**, open **Details & history** to read the teacher's feedback. Use **Edit**, **Save draft**, and **Submit** to revise and resubmit the same idea. After **Approve full specification work**, open **Details & history → Develop full specification**. Complete objectives, intended users, requirements, deliverables, scope, and dependencies; **Save specification** saves and closes the editor. Reopen **Details & history** and choose **Submit specification for acceptance review**. Permission to develop a specification is not catalogue acceptance; [a separate teacher decision](lehrkraefte.md#acceptance) is required before applications.

images.alt: Main idea returned for revision with teacher feedback
images.caption: This lifecycle includes an actual request for revision and resubmission.

images.alt: Complete submitted specification for the main idea
images.caption: The specification awaits a separate acceptance decision.

chapters.title: Review projects and save choices
chapters.text: An open [application period](administration.md#period) and at least three accepted projects are required. On `/applications`, **Accepted projects** lists eligible projects. Choose **Apply individually** or **Apply together**, then rank at least three distinct projects and save. This lifecycle uses three students and the shared group workflow. A submitted ranking is not a finalized allocation; students cannot see early preliminary runs.

images.alt: Application period configured for the synthetic project lifecycle
images.caption: The period has a bounded opening and deadline.

images.alt: Student's saved project ranking for the open application period
images.caption: The student submits real choices through the application interface.

chapters.title: Confirm the group and submit its proposal
chapters.text: After the deadline, allocation is finalized by an administrator. A preliminary result is not final membership. On `/applications`, **Assignment** shows the finalized group. On `/formal-application`, enter the eligible project and choose **Start a formal proposal**. Complete a topic, investigation concern, and planned result for every allocated member, plus the shared situation, objective, and milestones. Choose **Save draft**, then **Edit formal proposal** and **Submit for teacher review**. Only [formal teacher approval](lehrkraefte.md#formal-approval) authorizes project work.

images.alt: Administrator reviews and finalizes the completed allocation
images.caption: Finalization creates the membership used by the proposal workflow.

images.alt: Finalized School Garden Sensor group in the student account
images.caption: All three students belong to the group after finalization.

images.alt: Submitted official group proposal for the allocated project
images.caption: The official proposal is separate from the earlier project ranking.

chapters.title: View your assessment and project completion
chapters.text: After formal approval, use `/grading` to open your eligible project. Students see only their own individual grades; each assessment retains its routine or final phase, rubric version, date, and evidence. Teachers record [routine observations, final criterion assessments, and overall grades](lehrkraefte.md#grading) as separate decisions. On `/archive`, choose **Load private artefacts** and upload the website snapshot, poster, and source data with **Upload privately**. Check files for personal information and active content. **Request publication review** only submits a file for review. The anonymous archive appears only after [teacher review and project completion](lehrkraefte.md#completion).

images.alt: The signed-in group member's individual assessment with rubric version
images.caption: A student cannot view other members' individual grades.

lehrkraefte.title: Teacher guide
lehrkraefte.intro: Prerequisites: a teacher account and the existing authorization for each project. teacher01 reviews the main idea created by student01. Administrators do not make a teacher's academic decisions.

chapters.title: Review an idea and guide its revision
chapters.text: On `/ideas`, open the submitted main idea with **Review**. Choose **Decision → Request revision**, enter **Written feedback**, and select **Record decision**. After the student [revises and resubmits](schueler.md#revision), **Approve full specification work** allows specification development. **Decline** is an alternative. Optional ratings and **Overall recommendation** support the review but do not decide automatically. **Your supervision preference** is separate from approval. Teachers cannot review their own ideas.

images.alt: Teacher reviews another person's main idea and records a reasoned revision request
images.caption: The reviewer is not the idea's author.

chapters.title: Record or revise your supervision preference
chapters.text: On `/ideas`, choose **Details & history** for a project. Under **Your supervision preference**, choose **Wants to supervise** in **Preference**, then select **Save preference**. To revise it later, choose a different preference and save again. This records your interest in supervising and is separate from a review or approval decision.

images.alt: Teacher records Wants to supervise in the project details and history
images.caption: The saved supervision preference is separate from a review or approval decision.

chapters.title: Accept the completed specification
chapters.text: Review the submitted specification using **Work size**, **Curriculum relevance**, **Technical complexity**, **Feasibility**, **Learning value**, **Resource needs**, **Risk & dependencies**, and **Overall recommendation**. These fields are distinct from optional ratings in the initial idea review. **Accept for student applications** followed by **Record decision** makes the project available in the application catalogue. This is separate from the earlier approval to develop a specification. An administrator then [configures the period and supervision](administration.md#period).

images.alt: Teacher accepts the completed School Garden Sensor specification
images.caption: Acceptance makes the project eligible for student applications.

chapters.title: Approve the official group proposal
chapters.text: Prerequisites: finalized allocation and a submitted group proposal with member contributions and milestones. On `/formal-application`, select the project and review its topic, situation, objective, and decision history. Under **Teacher decision**, choose **Approve — group may begin**, enter reasoned **Feedback**, and select **Record teacher decision**. **Request revisions** and **Decline** are alternatives. Work is not authorized before approval.

images.alt: Teacher-approved official proposal with project work visibly authorized
images.caption: Approval applies to the project actually assigned to this group.

chapters.title: Record assessments, metrics, and final grades
chapters.text: Prerequisites: an approved project and [published rubric versions](administration.md#rubric). On `/grading`, select the project and explicitly choose the routine and final rubric versions independently; neither phase defaults to the globally active version. The student criterion editor lists every `STUDENT` or `BOTH` criterion in rubric order. Routine assessments start blank and save only rows with an explicitly chosen grade; each save appends observations. Final mode loads only this student's current final values for the selected final rubric, leaves unassessed rows blank, and requires a reason to revise a saved value. These criterion assessments are distinct from the **Final grades** controls for overall decisions. Use **Record group assessment** for a configured group criterion and **Record observation** for a configured metric; both remain routine-context inputs. History retains the phase and original rubric version. Preparation creates only the minimum overall final-grade records needed for the initial view; the teacher confirms the actual decision using **Save final project grade** and **Save individual final grade** with a rationale. Without a configured aggregation rule, a grade is a teacher decision, not an invented average or formula.

images.alt: Administrator's immutable rubric version with configured criteria and metrics
images.caption: The rubric is configuration, not an invented grading formula.

images.alt: Teacher view of a saved individual assessment and its evidence
images.caption: An assessment remains associated with the rubric version used to record it.

images.alt: Saved observation showing three documented model trials
images.caption: A metric is an observation, not an invented grade formula.

images.alt: Saved final grade with an explicit teacher rationale
images.caption: The teacher explains the decision; no calculation rule is invented.

chapters.title: Review private files and complete the project
chapters.text: On `/archive`, choose **Load private artefacts**. A private upload enters review only after **Request publication review**. **Approve publication** makes only the reviewed file public; **Reject** keeps it private. A synthetic control file remains deliberately unreviewed. Before completion, an authorized teacher may choose **Unpublish**; removable private files can be removed while the project remains active. After required files and final grades are ready, choose **Confirm project completion**. The archive is then read-only. Only a completed project has an anonymous `/archive/{projectId}` view. The approved snapshot download contains no identities, membership, applications, grades, feedback, private metrics, or audit data.

images.alt: Authenticated review shows approved files and a separate private control file
images.caption: File approval and project completion are separate actions.

images.alt: Anonymous completed-project archive containing only approved synthetic files
images.caption: The public view and downloads contain only approved synthetic content.

administration.title: Administration guide
administration.intro: Prerequisite: an administrator account. Administration manages accounts, catalogue entries, application periods, allocation, and rubric versions; it does not replace a teacher's academic decisions.

chapters.title: Manage accounts and classes
chapters.text: On `/admin`, **Users & roles** manages accounts. Registration creates student accounts and server-side authorization controls role changes. Under **Classes & subjects**, use **Add class** and **Add subject** to create entries and **Rename** to update an existing entry. Find the synthetic student account, choose **Edit**, select **Class**, mark up to four **Elective subjects**, and choose **Save**. Use synthetic testing accounts only; do not change their base roles for this guide. Students maintain their own display name in [settings](schueler.md#account).

images.alt: Administration view of synthetic accounts and class assignments
images.caption: Only authenticated administrators can manage accounts.

chapters.title: Configure the application period and supervision
chapters.text:
1. For this walkthrough, confirm a supervisor for its primary project: open `/ideas`, choose **Details & history** for that project, select a teacher under **Confirm supervisor**, and choose **Confirm supervisor**. This confirmation is part of the walkthrough; a confirmed supervisor is not required for a project to be included in an application period.
2. Open `/applications` and choose **＋ Configure period**. Enter **Label**, **School year**, **Opens at**, and **Closes at**. The closing time must be after the opening time and should reflect the intended application schedule for the school year; no production deadline duration is prescribed.
3. Choose the intended eligibility under **Who may apply**; this walkthrough uses **All students**. The walkthrough needs at least three [accepted projects](lehrkraefte.md#acceptance) for that school year. Select at least three accepted projects from the period's school year, including the project to be offered.
4. Choose **Create period**. Students then submit actual individual or group rankings before the deadline.

images.alt: Administrator configures the synthetic project application period
images.caption: The application period has a bounded opening and deadline.

chapters.title: Review and finalize allocation
chapters.text:
1. Open `/allocation` and select the configured period under **Application period**.
2. Wait for the deadline-triggered scheduler to produce its completed, non-early initial run. Do not start an early or replacement run as a substitute for this ordinary deadline workflow.
3. Choose **Inspect result** for that run and review the outcome before choosing **Finalize result**. Confirm the browser confirmation.
4. A completed preliminary result is not finalized membership; only after finalization should you rely on the resulting group membership or have students start their official proposal. The run uses the ordinary scheduler and finalization workflow; it does not override allocation behavior. The [student guide](schueler.md#allocation) follows that finalized group workflow.

images.alt: Administrator reviews a completed allocation before finalization
images.caption: The group proposal uses finalized memberships, not a preliminary run.

chapters.title: Publish an immutable rubric version
chapters.text: On `/rubrics`, view existing versions or start a local draft. Copy a saved version or load reusable UTF-8 JSON, edit the definition, and explicitly choose **Publish immutable version** with a unique version label. Copying, editing, and uploading are local only; they do not publish or activate anything. A published version is immutable, and earlier assessments retain their associated version. `/grading` is for project assessment and history. Only configured aggregation rules calculate results; this guide invents no formula. Continue to [teacher grading](lehrkraefte.md#grading).

images.alt: Immutable rubric version with configured assessment criteria and metrics
images.caption: Rubrics are managed separately from project assessment.
